gen-dafont-nordic-gf-pathway-extreme: Ancient, pinched, and stubborn: Nordic hammers out closed letters with a single steady stroke. Pathway Extreme replies with rounded, open shapes and a big x-height, and that openness is the strongest thing about the pair.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-preahvihear: A single constant-width line, traced tight and closed, gives Nordic its weathered, powerful look. Preahvihear sits opposite in open-mouthed sans-serif letters with a lofty x-height, so the page moves from cramped to breathing.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-prompt: Nordic brings a powerful, ancient heading with pinched, closed letters. Prompt, a sans-serif with oversized small letters and open apertures, would carry a long passage in a friendly, approachable way, without ever tiring the eye.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-pt-sans-caption: Chiseled and unshaded, Nordic spreads its constant strokes across the line like brush dabs set far apart. PT Sans Caption, a sans-serif with big, inviting bowls, settles in beneath.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-puritan: One monoline skeleton, pinched shut like a pressed leaf, defines Nordic. Puritan follows with rounded sans forms that stay open to the side, and that tension from tight to generous is what makes the pair work.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-questrial: Old and weighty, with tight closed forms and wide-set spacing, Nordic takes the top spot. Questrial moves in underneath as a plain sans with open curves and a tall band of letters, so the heading feels all the more carved.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-radio-canada: Nordic looks carved and ancient, its closed letters set far apart as if dabbed on with a brush. Radio Canada reads smoothly, with open curves and no pressure shifts.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-radio-canada-big: Powerful from the first letter, Nordic keeps its stroke monoweight and its openings pinched shut. And Radio Canada Big, a sans-serif with clear terminals and a tall x-height, leaves the heading to earn its keep big and brief.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro keeps a calm, unvarying weight from word to word, with broad gaps at every terminal. But over a longer passage it would read smoothly, a sans-serif quietly opposite to the cramped, ancient Nordic above.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-roboto: Roboto reads clean and open, its round letters generous. Set under Nordic's closed, ancient capitals, that gap in openness is the pair's strongest quality, and it gives the page two clear voices.
